statement: A subsequence of an array keeps some of its elements, possibly none or all, in their original order. An array of n elements has 2ⁿ subsequences, because each element is either picked or not picked.

The pick / not-pick recursion visits all of them: at index i, call once with nums[i] added to the current choice and once without it, and record the choice when i reaches n. Variations of this one pattern print every subsequence, stop at the first one that satisfies a condition, or count the ones that do.

Here you are given an integer array nums and an integer limit. Use the counting variation: return how many subsequences of nums have a sum of at most limit. The empty subsequence has sum 0, so it counts whenever limit ≥ 0.

examples.explanation: The subsequences with sum at most 3 are [], [1], [2], [3] and [1, 2]. Every other choice, such as [1, 3], adds up to more than 3.
Even the largest choice, [2, 4], sums to 6, so all 2² = 4 subsequences count.
